articles.title: Travis Kelce joins Cleveland Guardians ownership group as $1.7 billion MLB franchise adds a new chapter to his hometown legacy
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has built a successful career in the NFL, but his interests now extend beyond football.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has built a successful career in the NFL, but his interests now extend beyond football. In May 2026, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end became a minority investor in the Cleveland Guardians, giving him a financial connection to the Major League Baseball team he grew up supporting. The investment brings his professional success closer to his hometown roots, but questions remain about how much he paid, what percentage he owns, and whether his involvement could influence the franchise’s future. While the financial details remain private, the deal offers an interesting look at how professional athletes are turning their earnings and public profiles into long-term business investments.What do we know about Travis Kelce’s investment in the Cleveland Guardians?The Cleveland Guardians announced Kelce’s minority investment on May 27, 2026, marking a new chapter in the relationship between the NFL star and his hometown. The announcement came before the team’s game against the Washington Nationals, bringing attention to a deal that connected one of football’s most recognizable players with Cleveland’s baseball franchise.Kelce purchased a minority interest from the ownership group associated with David Blitzer. Blitzer holds a 35% stake in the Guardians, making his position an important part of the team’s ownership structure. However, this does not mean Kelce purchased 35% of the franchise. The reported transaction involved a portion of Blitzer’s interest, and the exact percentage acquired by Kelce has not been publicly disclosed.The distinction matters because ownership percentages determine the financial value of an investment and the rights that come with it. Without knowing Kelce’s exact share, it is not possible to establish his ownership value, calculate his expected returns, or determine how much of the team’s business he owns.The purchase price has also remained private. Neither Kelce nor the Guardians has announced the amount paid for the investment. As a result, figures circulating about his personal spending should not be treated as confirmed unless they can be supported by reliable reporting or an official disclosure.The transaction nevertheless gives Kelce a direct financial interest in a major professional baseball franchise. Instead of simply attending games or supporting the team as a celebrity fan, he now has a business connection to the organization.For Cleveland, the investment also brings an internationally recognized sports personality closer to the Guardians brand. Kelce’s NFL career, public appearances, and business activities give him a profile that extends beyond football. His involvement can attract attention to the baseball team, although the actual financial impact of that attention cannot be measured from the ownership announcement alone.How much are the Cleveland Guardians worth, and what could Kelce’s stake be worth?The Guardians’ reported valuation provides useful context for understanding why the investment has attracted attention. Forbes estimated the franchise’s value at approximately $1.7 billion around the time of the announcement, with other reports placing the figure in a similar range. The valuation reflects the broader business value of the franchise, rather than the amount Kelce paid for his individual share.The Guardians were valued at approximately $1 billion in 2022, when Blitzer first invested in the organization. Comparing that figure with the later estimate of roughly $1.7 billion suggests a substantial increase in the franchise’s reported value over four years.That rise is significant because professional sports teams can become valuable long-term assets. Their businesses are supported by several sources of income, including broadcasting agreements, ticket sales, sponsorships, merchandise, stadium-related revenue, and other commercial partnerships. The exact mix varies by franchise, and a team’s overall valuation does not mean all of that value is immediately available as cash to its owners.A higher franchise valuation can benefit existing investors if they eventually sell their shares at a favorable price. However, an increase in estimated value does not automatically translate into a realized profit. The final return depends on the purchase price, ownership percentage, operating costs, financial obligations, and the terms of a future sale.For Kelce, the absence of a disclosed ownership percentage makes it impossible to calculate a reliable value for his investment. For example, a hypothetical 1% interest in a franchise valued at $1.7 billion would correspond to $17 million before considering transaction terms and other adjustments. That is only an illustration of the mathematics, not a claim that Kelce owns 1% or invested $17 million.The same caution applies to estimates of how much money he might earn from the deal. The Guardians have not disclosed Kelce’s investment terms, any special financial arrangements, or the returns he could receive. It would therefore be inaccurate to describe a particular amount as his confirmed investment or expected profit.The most reliable conclusion is that Kelce has acquired an undisclosed minority interest in a franchise whose reported value is around $1.7 billion. That makes the deal potentially significant, but its precise financial value to him remains unknown.Will Travis Kelce have any control over the Guardians’ players and baseball decisions?Kelce’s investment does not make him the person responsible for running the Cleveland Guardians. His position as a minority investor is different from the role of a controlling owner, team president, general manager, or manager. These positions carry different responsibilities, and owning a portion of a franchise does not automatically give an investor authority over its baseball operations.The Dolan family remains the Guardians’ controlling ownership group. Its position is important because control of a sports franchise generally determines who has the final say over major organizational decisions. Kelce’s reported investment does not replace the existing ownership structure or give him control over the team.Decisions involving player contracts, trades, recruitment, coaching appointments, payroll, and long-term baseball strategy remain matters for the organization’s established leadership. There is no confirmed information indicating that Kelce will have direct authority over these decisions.This distinction is especially important when a celebrity becomes involved with a sports franchise. The public may associate a famous investor with the team and assume that the person will influence its future. In reality, an investor’s involvement depends on the rights attached to the shares they purchase and the agreements governing the ownership group.The Guardians have also been connected to a separate ownership development involving Blitzer. His 35% interest comes with an option to pursue majority control after the 2027 season. However, an option is not the same as a completed transaction. It gives its holder a potential route to a future deal, subject to the applicable terms, rather than guaranteeing that control will change hands.Kelce’s investment should therefore be understood within the existing ownership arrangement. His financial interest connects him to the franchise, but there is no confirmed basis for saying he will decide which players the Guardians sign, how much they spend on their roster, or who leads their baseball operations.His most visible contribution may instead come through his public profile and relationship with the city. A well-known athlete supporting a local team can attract media coverage, strengthen community connections, and introduce the franchise to audiences who might not regularly follow baseball. Those possibilities make the investment interesting without requiring Kelce to take on a management role.Why does the Guardians investment matter to Kelce’s hometown and his growing business portfolio?For Kelce, the Guardians investment carries a personal connection that goes beyond the financial value of the franchise. He grew up in Northeast Ohio and attended Cleveland Heights High School, where baseball was part of his sporting background before football became the centre of his professional career.His connection to Cleveland has remained part of his public identity even after establishing himself with the Kansas City Chiefs. The investment gives him a way to maintain that connection while participating in the business side of professional sports.The Guardians described Kelce as someone with a deep affection for Cleveland and Northeast Ohio. Kelce, in turn, presented the opportunity as a chance to strengthen his lasting connection with the city’s east side. These statements help explain the personal meaning of the deal, although they do not reveal its financial terms.The investment also fits into Kelce’s wider business activities. Beyond his NFL career, he has developed commercial interests and partnerships in areas such as entertainment, consumer brands, and sports. His business portfolio has included ventures associated with Garage Beer, investments connected to entertainment and hospitality, and the New Heights podcast, which he co-hosts with his brother, Jason Kelce.These activities show how a professional athlete can build income sources and business relationships beyond a playing contract. An athlete’s career on the field is limited by factors such as age, performance, injuries, and contract opportunities. Investments, by contrast, can potentially continue to hold value after the athlete retires, although they also carry financial risks.Owning a minority share of a baseball franchise offers a different opportunity from endorsing a product. An endorsement generally involves promoting a brand in exchange for compensation, while an equity investment gives the investor an ownership interest in a business. The potential financial outcome depends on the business’s performance, the value of the shares, and the terms of the investment.There may also be a branding benefit for the Guardians. Kelce’s popularity gives the team a connection to a major NFL audience, while his hometown background makes the relationship more meaningful to local supporters. However, it would be premature to assign a specific financial benefit to his involvement without evidence of increased ticket sales, sponsorship revenue, merchandise purchases, or other measurable results.Ultimately, the investment is both a business decision and a personal milestone for Kelce. It connects his professional success to a city that played an important role in his development and adds another dimension to his activities outside football.The central facts remain straightforward. Kelce became a minority investor in the Cleveland Guardians in May 2026, but the size and price of his stake have not been disclosed. The franchise has been valued at approximately $1.7 billion, while the Dolan family continues to hold the controlling position. articles.title: NFL Week 5 Schedule: How to Watch, TV Channels, Streaming, Game Previews
articles.summary: See the complete NFL Week 5 schedule, TV channels and streaming details for all 15 games, plus previews of the top matchups including six FOX games.
articles.body: Week 5 of the NFL regular season runs from Thursday, Oct. 8 through Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, and includes an International Series game in London, with the Eagles and Jaguars meeting at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. FOX carries six games this week, including a four-game window at 1 p.m. ET and a two-game window at 4:25 p.m. ET. Below is the complete Week 5 schedule with kickoff times and TV networks, followed by previews of the biggest matchups and everything you need to know about how to watch. NFL Week 5 Schedule Thursday, Oct. 8 Sunday, Oct. 11 Monday, Oct. 12 Four FOX games share the 1 p.m. ET window and two share the 4:25 p.m. ET window. The Eagles-Jaguars game in London kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET as part of the NFL's International Series. NFL Related Stories2026 NFL Power Rankings Week 5: Do 49ers Or Chiefs Hold Claim As NFL's Best Team?Monday Morning NFL Top 10 Rankings: New No. 1 After Hectic Week 4 SundayThe Long Road Back: NFL Ties League History With 5 Winless Teams Through Week 4 NFL Week 5 Game Previews Cincinnati Bengals at Miami Dolphins The Bengals are 2-2, while the Dolphins are 0-4. Miami looks for its first win of the season at home against a Cincinnati team that sits at .500. Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints The Vikings are 4-0 after their win over Miami on Sunday. They head to New Orleans to face the Saints inside the Superdome. New York Giants at Washington Commanders The Giants are 3-1, while the Commanders are 1-3. New York looks to build on its winning record against a Washington team trying to turn its season around. Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers The Bears are 3-1, while the Packers are 2-2. This NFC North rivalry game takes place at Lambeau Field. Detroit Lions at Arizona Cardinals The Lions are 2-2, while the Cardinals are 1-3. Arizona looks for its second win of the season at home against Detroit. San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks The 49ers are 4-0, while the Seahawks are 3-1. This NFC West matchup pits the 4-0 49ers against a 3-1 Seattle team. Want to watch every FOX game the rest of the season? Sign up for FOX One to stream every FOX NFL broadcast, including all six Week 5 games above, right from your phone, tablet or connected TV. Philadelphia Eagles at Jacksonville Jaguars The Eagles and Jaguars meet in London as part of the NFL's International Series. The Eagles are 2-2 and the Jaguars are 3-1, with an early-morning kickoff on NFL Network. Baltimore Ravens at Atlanta Falcons The Ravens are 3-1 and visit the Falcons on Sunday Night Football. Atlanta's record heading into this game was not yet final as of this writing, because the Falcons play their Week 4 game on Monday night. Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams The Bills are 3-1, while the Rams are 2-2. Buffalo travels to SoFi Stadium to close out the Week 5 slate on Monday Night Football. How to Watch NFL Week 5 FOX has six games in Week 5, including a four-game window at 1 p.m. ET and a two-game window at 4:25 p.m. ET. Because multiple FOX games overlap in each window, the exact matchup available in your market depends on your local broadcast map, so check local listings before kickoff. The Thursday night game between the Buccaneers and Cowboys airs exclusively on Prime Video. The Eagles-Jaguars International Series game from London airs on NFL Network at 9:30 a.m. ET. CBS carries five Sunday games, including the Broncos-Chargers game at 4:05 p.m. ET. The Ravens-Falcons Sunday night game airs on NBC and streams on Peacock. The Monday night Bills-Rams game airs on ABC and ESPN. More NFL Coverage This Week Catch up on the latest from around the league before Week 5 kicks off Thursday night. articles.title: Sophie Cunningham's insufferable ex-teammate mouths off but can't make a shot, ref lowers his shoulder & Ditka
articles.summary: Another Friday Nightcaps digs into Sydney Colson's profane rant telling Sophie Cunningham to shut up about transgender athletes, plus her WNBA stats.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Another Friday. We're here. We've made it! While the left spent all week whining about Sophie Cunningham's hat and firing squad best practices, us PATRIOTS were biding our time, keeping our heads down, and grinding towards another weekend. And now, we're here. And there ain't a thing they can do about it. Let's roll. Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham's ex-teammate, Sydney Colson, virtue-signals her BUTT off while also having maybe the worst career stats I've ever seen. SPORTS MEDIA OUTLET CONSIDERS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM MORE POLARIZING THAN MEGAN RAPINOE Seriously. This is who's telling Sophie — and white people — to shut up? The WNBA can do better than this, right? Right?! What else? I've got Dak getting heckled by an Uber driver, a referee absolutely trucking a poor soul on the sidelines, and I'm sad about Mike Ditka. What an awful year for deaths. I feel like we say that every year, but goodness, 2026 has been a real kick to the you-know-whats in terms of death. And we still have three months to go! Brutal. On that happy note, grab you a slice of sausage pizza ahead of Sunday's National Sausage Pizza Day, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap! This is the best they got? Really? I've got no real hot takes on pizza beyond the fact that I do, in fact, believe sausage is the best topping. I'm not just saying that because of the occasion. It's the best, by a mile. Mount Rushmore of Pizza Toppings to kick this Friday class off? Sure. Why not?! Meatballs as a topping are underrated in the pizza topping game. They're not on every menu, but when they are, HAMMER it. You are welcome! And that concludes our Ted Talk portion of today's class. NOW, let's officially get the day started with some ex-WNBA player named Sydney Colson pandering to the left by telling Sophie Cunningham and her white counterparts to PIPE DOWN. Amazing: At least she backed up her talk on the floor! Listen, if you never speak up about a d–n thing when you know it’s impacting the people that you claim to love, care about, you know we’re fighting together as a team, sister, blah blah blah, and you don’t speak up when things affect them. They don’t respect you. They are just trying to make it. Let me just tell you now, for real, for real: For the white players in the league, when you don’t say s–t, and even worse, when you say things that are harmful, talking about the trans s–t, nobody respects you. Shut the f–k up. Shut the f–k up. Nobody wants to hear your opinion. Freedom of speech, so you can say it, but just know people are just trying to get by when they’re dealing with you. And you ought to be ashamed. Y’all ought to be ashamed to act like you’re cool with people, to act like you care about sisterhood, all of these things. Again, it's just amazing. These "athletes" are just incredible. They're the gifts that keep on giving "the whole year," as Cousin Eddie would say. As Dan Z. said in the above post, let's quickly remind everyone of the VERY HARMFUL thing Sophie Cunningham told ESPN months ago as it pertains to trans people: "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men." That's it! THAT's what Sydney Colson, who played with Cunningham last season in Indiana, deems "harmful" rhetoric. Speaking of last season, because I had never heard of this girl before this morning, I decided to do some Big J digging to see if her play on the court warranted all this chest-pumping off of it. It ... did not: Dak, Mike & what a hit! Well, there you have it. That's who is calling out Sophie Cunningham. A player who struggled to score three points per game during her illustrious career in the WNBA. Okeedokee! By the way, for the "Sophie stinks, too!" crowd ... she's averaged at least 8 points per game off the bench every year since 2022, including two seasons in double-digits. She's also a top-five three-point shooter in the league. It ain't close. OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL! To hype everyone up, let's start off with a ref in last night's South Alabama-Arkansas State game lowering his shoulder on a 100-yard kick return: BOOOOM! You don't often see a referee doing the trucking, right? Usually, we're watching those guys get pummeled. Frankly, it's a nice change of pace for the Zebras. I've spent all year ragging on them — for good reason. They've generally stunk at all levels. But credit where it's due here. This guy had a job to do, and he wasn't gonna let some innocent bystander stand in his way. Nicely done. Next? Speaking of (not so) innocent bystanders ... So, Dak and the Cowboys put up their annual primetime clunker last night, and this was the big story that came out of it ... Someone — boots on the ground say the guy was a driver — called Dak "embarrassing" after he threw two picks in a loss to the winless Buccaneers, and he took exception to it. I say fair on both accounts, by the way. The guy was pissed. He was clearly a fan. Dak stunk. It was embarrassing. Dak also has a right to turn his head around and get pissed. I would, too. And if the guy really did turn his head around after saying it, and then doubled down AFTER Dak looked away, it is kind of a wussy move. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! If you're gonna say something, say it! Don't be a keyboard warrior. Man up, call Dak out for his stinker, and let the chips fall where they may. OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. Solid week. And now we get to enjoy three straight nights of football. What a blessing. What a country. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER It's only fitting to let the late Mike Ditka take us home. RIP to a legend.

articles.title: Shocking suspensions, f-bombs and a flurry of flags. What's going on with NFL officiating and what's next?
articles.summary: The league pressed the officiating union for more accountability measures ahead of the new CBA. And the league just suspended two officials a full eight seas...
articles.body:
With 1:48 to play in the first half of the New England Patriots-Buffalo Bills game on Sunday, the officiating crew made an announcement.

"Unsportsmanlike conduct, head coach for New England."

The Bills were awarded half the distance to the goal in yardage that would set them up for a game-tying touchdown less than a minute later.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, upon hearing the officials, looked taken aback. Penalty yards for telling the official that a defensive holding flag was a "f***ing terrible f***ing call"?

"I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said after the Patriots' 29-26 win . "There was nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive …

"I probably shouldn't have swore. But I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that."

By day's end, the comments of Vrabel — one of six head coaches currently serving on the NFL's competition committee — would take on heightened import.

Because across the league, tension between officials and players hit a rare high last week. Line judge Jeff Seeman, in view of a broadcasting camera, told Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride "f*** you." Referee Adrian Hill appeared to motion demonstratively and emotionally at Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson after a tangle with Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon knocked Wilson into Hill, who fell to the ground. (Wilson appeared to offer Hill a hand to get up.)

The suspensions, against the backdrop of Vrabel's public comments that he has regularly used profanity in interacting with officials, beg the question: What is the threshold of acceptable conduct from officials toward players and coaches, and in reverse? How should the system work and what explains the seeming increase in tension through the NFL's first four weeks?

Yahoo Sports canvassed league sources to better understand the dynamic of an often-charged relationship that seems tenser than usual. What awaits the rest of the season?

"It's a really tough job to be a ref," Pittsburgh Steeler wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. told Yahoo Sports by Zoom this week . "They take a lot of verbal abuse from coaches, players, fans. So definitely it's not for the thin-skinned."

After refs union calls suspension 'excessive and inconsistent,' league sources reiterate 'expectation' for officials in heated moments

It's impossible to determine how and whether contentious collective bargaining agreement (CBA) negotiations between the NFL and officials this spring have trickled over into the early weeks of the season.

Ask some team and league executives, and they'll say it's coincidence that these suspensions occurred the same week and coincidence this timed with multiple high-profile coaches questioning officiating.

Ask others, and the proximity of this tension to the league threatening replacement officials seems "impossible" to deny, in the word of one NFC executive.

What is clear: The league pressed the officiating union for more accountability measures ahead of the new CBA. And the league just suspended two officials a full eight seasons after the last known officiating suspension.

Before this week, the last known officiating suspension (officially an "administrative leave") was Roy Ellison's 2018 due to an official-player confrontation. Side judge Rob Vernatchi was suspended one game in 2015 due to a game-clock error, and Ellison was also suspended one game in 2013 after profanity against a player. Before that, the last suspension dated back to 1984 in response to an official's conduct toward fans.

So suspending two officials in a season, much less in one week, is unusual.

The officiating union issued a Tuesday statement saying it would "challenge the severity of those suspensions and meet with the NFL Officiating Department to discuss the League's disciplinary standards."

"NFL officials have a responsibility to conduct themselves professionally on the field, and the actions in these incidents fell short of that standard," NFL Referees Association executive director Scott Green said. "Accountability matters, but that should not result in discipline that is excessive or inconsistent with established precedent."

Coaches and players can, via flag and fine, receive discipline for their words and actions toward officials. This most often occurs if a player or coach repeatedly tests the boundaries with an official in a game, officials often warning coaches or players before issuing more discipline.

League sources do not believe frustration with a player or coach warrants a heated response.

"If they think somebody crosses the line, then they can drop the flag," one league source with knowledge of officiating discussions told Yahoo Sports. "Ultimately, the expectation is that these guys should not be in altercations and should walk away from it."

Neither Seeman nor Hill did that. Add to that bye weeks reducing the number of officials needed in Week 5 and Week 6 relative to the first four weeks, and the officiating bench now offering a deeper roster since the signing of the CBA, and the league chose to act at a rate it hasn't in league history.

Less-drastic accountability, league sources say, is not unusual. Each week, each official is graded not only on the consistency and accuracy of their calls, but also on behavioral considerations such as their field positioning, administration, mechanics, communication and speed. Those grades influence playoff assignments, with the most successful officials earning the highest-profile and most-coveted matchups. (The union sought to negotiate playoff assignments based on seniority rather than performance in the spring, and the league did not budge.)

Some coaches and players approach officials before a game to discuss their top concerns about their opponents' flag worthiness as well as ask for clarity on how a call will be officiated. Others try to minimize their interactions with officials and hope for the best.

"I don't like to talk to the refs," Pittman said, speaking in partnership with Toyota NFL FLAG. "They make me mad. When I was a younger player, I used to bark at them. But I always found that to come back and bite me.

"So now I just bite my tongue. I don't say anything."

Sources split on best response to rash of flags, high-profile calls

There are times, as it relates to officiating, that coaches and players are instructed not to say anything.

A defensive pass interference call in the final two minutes of the Los Angeles Rams' loss to the Denver Broncos brought that conversation back into public focus.

With 1:15 to play in the fourth quarter, Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was called for pass interference on a Bo Nix pass intended for Pat Bryant. The Broncos scored the game-winning touchdown after the drive stayed alive, and officials told Rams head coach Sean McVay in the days that followed that they agreed Wallace did not actually commit pass interference. McVay acknowledged that admission after he was asked about it multiple times during his news conference that week.

The league responded by sending a memo to teams reminding them conversations on officiating reviews are expected to be confidential.

"If something's obvious and the whole world wants to know 'hey, what ultimately happened?' then you've got to address it …" a high-ranking NFC executive told Yahoo Sports." But rehashing, that'd be like saying, 'OK, we're going to go over every grade of every player in the NFL last weekend and we're going to show it to the fans.' Is that transparency? I don't know.

McVay said he was focused more on the coaching point moving forward.

"The only thing that matters to me is how to educate our players," said McVay, who is also on the competition committee. "What I am interested in is if there's any sort of feedback that says this is in alignment with what would be correctly officiated as a DPI?

"That's the only thing that I'm really worried about."

League sources were split on whether there's reason to worry more broadly about officiating calls and conduct as Week 5 is underway.

On one hand, per ESPN data , the NFL saw the most accepted penalties through four weeks since play-by-play data became available in 1978. The 271 accepted penalties in Week 4 marked the second-most of any week in that span, per ESPN.

Others in the league counter that measuring "accepted" penalties rather than called penalties skews officials' performances. After all, officials don't choose whether to accept penalties. And some accepted penalties, like delay of game, can reflect strategy rather than overzealous officiating.

Delay of game and false start penalties are each at 10-year highs, per NFL data . More than half of the 63 delay-of-game penalties are on fourth down, when teams strategically prompt it, while an uptick in false starts could reflect the increased use of presnap motion by league offenses. The decrease in preseason participation by starters also has led to some less-disciplined play in recent years.

"You can't look at one penalty in abstract," a high-ranking team executive countered when told this information. "You have to look at game flow and what's actually being called and what's determining it. Because ultimately, that's what people were responding to."

NFL team owners and executives will meet Oct. 20 and 21 in New York City to discuss a range of issues with an agenda that historically has included officiating updates. It's rare any officiating or rule changes would occur during the season, though the NFL and NFL Players Association have already worked to clarify and reduce touchdown celebration penalties after a rash of fines.

Solutions league sources are interested in exploring: grant coaches one challenge flag to be used on currently unreviewable calls like defensive pass interference; issue two-minute reports of late-game officiating like the NBA does; allow broadcasts to stream the audio of officiating conversations as NCAA and UFL games do.

NBA and MLB each allow a coach's/manager's challenge per game, with stipulations; NHL allows coaching challenges as well albeit with penalty for incorrect challenges.

In the short term, it's unlikely any changes will occur. Multiple league sources predicted these suspensions, paired with the typical adjustment of players and coaches as a season elapses, will be enough to return officiating to perhaps not popular levels but at least normal ones.

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur and Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell each expressed a desire to move past the incidents between their respective players and officials. LaFleur added that "I do want to give the man a little bit of grace."

Vrabel knows he, too, will need to watch his language and positioning after referee Bill Vinovich told a pool reporter that Vrabel leaving the box and cursing prompted "pretty much a given" penalty.

"I apologized to him," Vrabel said. "Again, players responded [to the penalty yardage]. It was unfortunate. And I have to be better in those moments."

images.caption: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel shares a moment with referee Bill Vinovich in Week 4. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)
This incident between referee Adrian Hill and Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson resulted in a suspension for the official. (Stephen Maturen via Getty Images)

articles.title: Eagles rule out RB Saquon Barkley, WR DeVonta Smith, along with member of new-look OL, ahead of London game vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Across the pond, Philadelphia will be down its leading rusher and receiver, plus its new center.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will be playing in a different country Sunday with a vastly different offensive lineup than the one they trotted out for Week 1 last month.

Against the 3-1 Jacksonville Jaguars in London this weekend, the 2-2 Eagles will be without their leading rusher and receiver, as well as a member of their new-look offensive line. Running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith will be sidelined with hamstring injuries. Due to a knee issue, Drew Kendall, who started the past three games at center, also won't be able to play.

Wideout Hollywood Brown (ankle) is also out and so is safety Marcus Epps (groin). Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is questionable.

On the bright side for the Eagles, they're getting tight end Dallas Goedert and linebacker Zack Baun back. Goedert missed the last two outings with a knee problem. A concussion kept Baun from competing in last week's loss to the Los Angeles Rams .

Still, the pressure will be on quarterback Jalen Hurts to generate offense despite key losses. After all, Philadelphia's offensive line has morphed midseason, particularly this week.

Six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson suddenly retired on Tuesday . On Wednesday, the Eagles traded two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens for draft compensation , namely a 2028 second-round pick. Jurgens had been filling in at left guard in the absence of three-time Pro Bowler Landon Dickerson, who went on injured reserve with a knee issue after the season opener .

Kendall, meanwhile, took Jurgens' place at center. His performance there has impressed general manager Howie Roseman . But the 2025 fifth-round pick from Boston College won't be available Sunday against the Jags.

That means Philadelphia will be missing three of its O-line starters from Weeks 2-3.

Former undrafted free agent Jake Majors, a second-year Texas product, appeared to be filling Kendall's void during practice Thursday, as captured by ESPN's Tim McManus . Majors was signed to the Eagles' active roster from their practice squad Friday.

Another undrafted player from the 2025 class is expected to slot in at left guard for the time being: Willie Lampkin.

Lampkin could be a short-term solution at the position until Dickerson returns from IR. Johnson's heir at right tackle is rookie Markel Bell, a third-rounder Philadelphia selected out of Miami.

The Eagles' transformed O-line will be blocking for not only Hurts but also a backfield that'll be down Barkley, as well as backup running back Tank Bigsby , the latter of whom landed on IR and needed core muscle surgery.

Will Shipley will likely be in for an increased workload on the ground. He'll be joined by a pair of practice squad backs: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. They've been elevated this week.

Pierce's presence in the league has faded in recent years, but he rushed for 939 yards as a rookie with the Houston Texans in 2022. As for Steele, he made three starts for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 and wrapped that season with 183 yards on 56 totes.

articles.title: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles suffers health scare after taking helmet to the stomach during celebration
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles took a helmet to the stomach during celebrations and went down to a knee while grimacing in pain.
articles.body: Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles had every reason to celebrate after his team pulled off an impressive upset win over the Dallas Cowboys. So, when he was seen grimacing in pain on the sideline while down on one knee as the clock wound down on the Bucs’ 24-16 win Thursday at AT&T Stadium, it was an alarming scene. However, it turns out the 62-year-old was in pain because he took a helmet to the stomach during the Buccaneers’ celebration after they intercepted Dak Prescott to help seal the win, according to ESPN. Bowles said he will be OK moving forward, according to the report. articles.title: Former Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Rob Havenstein hunts, kills massive bear in Alaska
articles.summary: Super Bowl champ Rob Havenstein's Alaska hunting photos reveal a massive brown bear that completely dwarfs the retired Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman.
articles.body: While most people spend their retired years relaxing on a beach somewhere or RV-ing across the country, former Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Rob Havenstein had different ideas. The recently retired Super Bowl champion recently went on a hunting trip in Alaska, and while you'd assume some of his trophies would include moose or elk, Havenstein was feeling a little more bold. The 34-year-old former left tackle posted a carousel of photos from the trip on his official Instagram page on Thursday, and the main focus of the hunting trip was an absolutely massive brown bear. CODY JOHNSON FIRES BACK AT CRITICS, CALLS ALASKA GRIZZLY BEAR HUNT A 'CONSERVATIONIST EFFORT' And when I say "massive," I mean you're probably not ready for the size of this thing. There aren't many living things on this planet that can make an NFL offensive tackle look tiny, but this majestic creature absolutely dwarfs Havenstein in every picture it's in. FAT BEAR WEEK BRACKET IS SET: MEET THE HEAVYWEIGHTS, UNDERDOGS AND DEFENDING CHAMP IN THIS YEAR'S TOURNAMENT "I knew when I retired that I wanted to go somewhere wild, experience something outside of my comfort zone and chase incredible critters," Havenstein wrote in his post. "Alaskan Brown Bear presented that opportunity." "The main goal was obviously to hunt a mature brown bear, but what I took home with me was so much more than that. Appreciation for these incredible animals and the beautiful habitat they live in." Havenstein goes on to thank everyone that helped him in his hunt while dedicating the second half of his Instagram carousel to the other parts of his Alaskan trip. There are pictures of the lake he fished on, the massive wild salmon he caught, and his camping situation. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. articles.title: Travis Kelce-owned $1.7 billion franchise gets major boost from $53,690 charity donation
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s growing connection to Cleveland sports has taken on added significance as the Cleveland Guardians continue to strengthen their community
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s growing connection to Cleveland sports has taken on added significance as the Cleveland Guardians continue to strengthen their community ties. Express Wash Concepts (EWC), the parent company of Clean Express Auto Wash, has raised $53,690 for Cleveland Guardians Charities through its annual fundraising campaign. The donation highlights how a local business partnership can turn everyday purchases into meaningful support for young people and families. Kelce, who joined the Guardians’ ownership group as a minority investor in May 2026, also has a personal connection to the team and the city where he grew up.Cleveland Guardians Charities receives $53,690 donationEWC announced the contribution on June 23, 2026, following its fifth annual CLE Inspires campaign. The fundraising drive centred on a special three-day promotion that encouraged customers to purchase the limited-time Guardians Shine + Ceramic car wash. A portion of every sale went towards Cleveland Guardians Charities.The latest campaign delivered a substantial increase over the previous year. In 2025, EWC donated $28,450 to the charity. The 2026 total of $53,690 nearly doubled that amount, reflecting strong customer participation and support from employees.John Roush, founder and CEO of Express Wash Concepts, credited the communities the company serves for helping the initiative grow.“Our customers and team members continue to show what’s possible when a community comes together around a great cause,” said John Roush, founder and CEO of EWC.“This year’s campaign nearly doubled last year’s contribution, which speaks volumes about the generosity of the communities we serve. At EWC, we’re committed to making a meaningful impact beyond the wash, and we’re honored to partner with Cleveland Guardians Charities to help create more opportunities for local youth and families.”The contribution forms part of EWC Cares, the company’s wider community programme. Its efforts include fundraising events, sponsorships, donation drives and grants for organisations working in areas such as education, youth development, health and family support.EWC was also accepting applications for its 2026 community grants through October 31, offering another opportunity for eligible organisations to seek support.Travis Kelce’s Cleveland Guardians investment adds a hometown connectionKelce’s involvement with the Guardians gives the charity partnership another point of interest. In May 2026, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end joined the Major League Baseball franchise’s ownership group as a minority investor. The Cleveland Heights native grew up supporting Cleveland sports, making the investment a personal milestone rather than simply another business venture.The ownership move reflects Kelce’s long-standing affection for his hometown. While the percentage of his stake and the purchase price have not been publicly disclosed, his investment gives him a direct connection to the organisation beyond his years as a fan.Meanwhile, Clean Express Auto Wash operates 58 locations across Cleveland, Detroit, Toledo and Pittsburgh. Its partnership with the Guardians demonstrates how businesses can use sports promotions to engage customers while supporting community initiatives.For Cleveland Guardians Charities, the latest donation provides additional resources for its work with local youth and families. articles.title: Browns Called Top Trade Destination for 1,000-Yard Bucs RB
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns called top trade destination for Bucs' 1,000-yard running back. The post Browns Called Top Trade Destination for 1,000-Yard Bucs RB appeared...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed free-agent running back Kenneth Gainwell as an expensive alternative to presumed starter Bucky Irving after injury issues kept him sidelined for most of 2025.

Irving has come out of the gate looking like one of the NFL's best running backs—just like his rookie year in 2024—while Gainwell has largely been an afterthought on a 2-year, $14 million contract.

Bleacher Report's Alex Ballentine thinks that if the Buccaneers continue to spiral after a 1-4 start, Gainwell could be an attractive trade option for a playoff hopeful.

In this case, a surprise playoff hopeful — the Cleveland Browns.

"Targeting secondary backs who help in the passing game," Ballentine wrote on October 9. "Targeting Kenneth Gainwell would just be a more experienced version of that kind of back."

Gainwell had over 1,000 yards of total offense with the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2025.

Kenneth Gainwell Called NFL's Top Backup RB

ESPN's Bill Barnwell put Gainwell at the top of his list of the NFL's top backup running backs in the preseason.

"One of 2025's most productive backs on a per-touch basis, Gainwell averaged 4.7 yards per carry on the ground and caught 73 passes as an outlet for Aaron Rodgers ," Barnwell wrote on July 20. "He was sixth in the NFL in success rate (47.4%) among RBs with 100 or more carries, while his explosive play rate (9.6%) was right around league average. He is another back perfectly suited for a rotational role, and he'll compete with Dowdle to be our RB1."

Kenneth Gainwell Made Big Offseason Impression

Following Tampa Bay's mandatory minicamp, Pewter Report's Bailey Adams singled out Gainwell as a player who jumped off the page.

"Veteran running back Kenny Gainwell, a newcomer to the Bucs offense, was a major standout," Adams wrote on June 18. "During 7-on-7 work, he caught a fade for a touchdown from Baker Mayfield , going up to make a leaping catch before falling to the ground and securing the ball … getting a lot of the reps with the starters due to Bucky Irving's recovery from injury, Gainwell shined both as a runner and as a pass catcher. But it was his work in the passing game that stood out the most. It really looks like he'll be a big part of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson."

Irving was a sensation as a rookie, with 1,514 yards of total offense and 8 touchdowns, including 1,122 rushing yards, while serving mostly as a backup to Rachaad White .

In 2025, Irving had 865 total yards and 4 touchdowns.

articles.title: Seahawks have a fun challenge on their hands with 49ers' Brock Purdy
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks and the San Francisco 49ers are gearing up for a high-contest game.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks are trying hard to get back to the big game and be one of the new NFL franchises to notch back-to-back championship wins, and so far, they're 3-1, so they're getting there. But they obviously have a challenge up against the San Francisco 49ers .

The 49ers are undefeated going into Week 5, and they're No. 1 in the NFC West. There's no denying that quarterback Brock Purdy is just playing good football, and that's tough to top. But the Seahawks can do it, and one way is by finally sacking Purdy.

In a Friday feature, ESPN released its predictions for the NFL Week 5 schedule of games. In it, they mention a fun fact that Purdy actually has yet to be sacked this season. So, consider it a fun challenge for the Seahawks' defense to be the first to sack him.

Brock Purdy has yet to be sacked this season

"When the Seahawks beat the 49ers in Week 18 and in the divisional round of the playoffs last season, their defense held San Francisco to a combined 409 yards and nine points," Brady Henderson of ESPN notes. "That was then. The 49ers' offense now? Second in the NFL in scoring at 30.5 points per game, and QB Brock Purdy has yet to take a sack."

Ahead of the Seahawks and 49ers game, Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said of Purdy, "He can throw at all three levels. He throws on time. He throws it into windows with timing that makes it hard to defend."

Listen, so long as nobody gets hurt, sacking the other team's quarterback is a good thing. So, perhaps the Seahawks will be the first team in the 2026-27 season to do so.
